resources.string: A simple private diary for periods. It helps you remember dates and gives a careful guess about what may happen next. All data stays on your device.
Choose the closest answer. You can change it later. This helps the app avoid giving false exact dates.
My periods started less than 1 year ago
In the first year, periods often come at uneven times. That can be normal. The app will use a wide date range instead of pretending it knows an exact day.
During the first few years, periods can still come earlier or later from month to month. The app will allow for that.
My periods have been coming for more than 3 years
The app will learn from your recent dates. If your periods are fairly similar, its date range can become narrower.
My periods are changing as I get older
As periods get closer to stopping for good, they may come earlier, later, or skip months. The app will use a wider range and will not guess an egg-release day.
I have had no period for 12 months or more
The app will stop guessing the next period. If bleeding starts after a full year without periods, it is important to tell a doctor.
Choose the first day when the bleeding looked like your usual period, not just a few spots.
About how many days are there\nbetween your periods?
Count from the first day of one real period to the first day of the next. For example, from the 1st to the 29th is 28 days.
It is fine if you are not sure. Pick the closest number you know. The app will learn from the dates you add.

Because you have had no period for 12 months or more, My Cycle will keep your diary but will not guess when another period should come. New bleeding after a full year without periods should be checked by a doctor.
day since the last period started
This is only a count of days. It does not tell us exactly what your body is doing today.
Your next period may start around
The app is keeping your records without trying to guess a next period.
This is a rough first guess. Add more real dates and the app will learn your pattern.
Your dates can change quite a lot, so the app shows a wider range instead of one exact day.
This range is based on your recent recorded periods. It is still only a guess.
Days when pregnancy may be more likely
You are inside the rough calendar range
This is only a calendar guess. The app cannot know exactly when an egg is released. Never use these dates as “safe days” to avoid pregnancy.
Your periods started recently. In the first year it is common for them to come at uneven times. Keep recording the real dates; the app will not force them into a 28-day pattern.
In the first few years, periods can still come earlier or later from month to month. Keep recording what really happens.
As periods get closer to stopping for good, the gaps between them often change. The app therefore uses a wide date range and does not guess an egg-release day.
You chose “no period for 12 months or more”. The app will not guess another period. If new bleeding appears after a full year without periods, tell a doctor.
There was a gap of about 3 months or more between periods. In the first years after periods begin, such a long gap is worth discussing with a doctor or another trusted health professional.
A new period was recorded after about a year or more without one. Please tell a doctor about this bleeding, even if it is light.
This gap between periods is outside the range that is common for this stage. One unusual month does not give a diagnosis, but if it keeps happening or worries you, talk to a doctor.
Around the middle of the cycle
This is a rough place in the calendar, not a test of what your body is doing.
An egg may be released around this part of some cycles, but a calendar cannot tell the exact day.
This is the later part of the calendar cycle. The exact timing can change.
Pale colors are guesses from past dates. Your body does not have to follow them.
Choose “A few spots” when there is only a little blood and it does not look like your usual period. A few spots will not start a new cycle in the app.
Write anything you want to remember…
Shortest and longest differ by about %1$d days
There are not enough finished cycles yet. Keep adding real dates.
In the first year after periods begin, uneven gaps are common. The numbers below are a diary summary, not a rule your body must follow.
During the first few years, the gaps can still change. The app shows what happened instead of judging it against a 28-day cycle.
These numbers describe your own recent history. If your pattern suddenly changes or worries you, the app cannot tell you why.
When periods are getting closer to stopping for good, the gaps often change and skipped months become more common. The app will not treat that as a clockwork cycle.
You chose “no period for 12 months or more”. The history stays here, but the app does not guess another period.
Choose what fits now. You can change this at any time without deleting old records.

A private period diary that learns from your own dates. It shows ranges instead of claiming to know an exact next period or egg-release day. It is not a medical test.
Your period records stay on this device unless you choose to save a CSV copy
